intro: Be. is at 206 Flatbush Avenue on the Park Slope and Prospect Heights border, a block from the Bergen Street 2 and 3 station and a short walk from Barclays Center. It is the larger of the two licensed dispensaries we track in Park Slope, with about 370 products from 39 brands. Vapes lead at 113 listings, followed by 99 flower options and 82 pre-rolls. Edibles are a smaller 54, and there is an 11-item concentrate case.

The brand list is different from most New York shops. Find. is the deepest at 38 products, with ISH and Select at 35 each, then Grassroots, RYTHM and Cheetah, a mix that leans toward multi-state producers and flower. There are no $5 drinks here: the entry price is $11 for Find. pre-rolls in Bluejack, Crusty Crustacean, B.A.M. and Mint Snackz. For gummies and drinks, Verdi's Park Slope store on 7th Avenue is the better pick; for flower and vapes near Barclays, Be. has the deeper shelf.
know: About 370 products from 39 brands; vapes (113) and flower (99) lead.
Find., ISH, Select and Grassroots are the main brands, a multi-state-heavy mix.
Entry price is $11 for Find. single pre-rolls; no sub-$10 drinks or tablets listed.
Verdi Park Slope on 7th Avenue is the other licensed shop in the neighborhood.

faq.q: Is Be. close to Barclays Center?
faq.a: Yes. It is on Flatbush Avenue a few blocks south of the arena and Atlantic Terminal, with the Bergen Street 2 and 3 station a block away. Note that you cannot consume cannabis inside the arena or on its plaza.

faq.q: Why is the cheapest item $11?
faq.a: Be. does not list the $5 single-serve drinks or low-dose tablets that set the floor at most New York shops. Its lowest-priced items are Find. pre-rolls at $11 before tax. The edible selection is also small at 54 listings.

faq.q: Does Be. have a good flower selection?
faq.a: Yes for its size. With 99 flower listings and Grassroots, RYTHM and Find. stocked, it has more loose flower than Verdi Park Slope and a mix of New York and out-of-state growers.

intro: Verdi's Chelsea store is at 158 West 23rd Street, between 6th and 7th Avenues, steps from the 23rd Street F, M and 1 stations. It carries about 350 products from 75 brands, the smallest of the six licensed dispensaries we track in Chelsea and Flatiron but with one of the longer brand lists. Vapes lead at 99 listings, with 93 edibles, 72 pre-rolls and 56 flower options, plus 19 concentrates and 11 tinctures.

MFNY is the deepest brand at 25 products, and PAX, Jaunty, Wyld, Back Home Cannabis Co. and Rove follow. The entry price is $7.91 for Foy's four-pack sleep chews with adaptogens, and 5 Boro dime bags of Fuel Pump and Cereal Milk flower and Nanticoke's Durban Poison joint are all $10.17. Verdi also runs a Park Slope store in Brooklyn. In Chelsea, Stoops and Alchemy are larger menus a few blocks west, so Verdi is the pick for a quick, brand-diverse stop right at the 23rd Street subway.
know: About 350 products from 75 brands; vapes (99) and edibles (93) lead.
MFNY, PAX, Jaunty and Wyld are the deepest brands; 19 concentrates and 11 tinctures.
Entry price is $7.91 for Foy sleep chews; 5 Boro dime bags of flower are $10.17.
Steps from the 23rd Street F, M and 1 stations; Stoops and Alchemy are larger nearby.

faq.q: What is a dime bag at Verdi?
faq.a: 5 Boro sells small single-gram-scale flower bags listed at $10.17 before tax, in strains like Fuel Pump and Cereal Milk. It is one of the cheaper ways to try loose flower in Manhattan without buying an eighth.

faq.q: Is Verdi Chelsea the same as Verdi Park Slope?
faq.a: Same operator, separate menus. The Chelsea store lists about 350 products and the Park Slope store about 235. Brand lists overlap, with MFNY deep at both, but stock and prices differ.

faq.q: Does Verdi carry tinctures?
faq.a: Yes, 11 listings, which is more than most Chelsea shops. Tinctures are sublingual oils dosed by the dropper, useful if you want a measured, smoke-free option that acts faster than a gummy.

intro: The Flowery's Brooklyn store is at 692 Grand Street in Williamsburg, near Manhattan Avenue on the east side of the neighborhood, close to the Grand Street L station. It lists about 350 products from 59 brands, the second-largest of the six licensed dispensaries we track in Williamsburg behind Gotham's Domino location. Vapes lead at 104 listings, with 95 pre-rolls, 70 edibles and 65 flower options and an 11-item concentrate case.

Jaunty is the deepest brand at 25 products, followed by STIIIZY, MFNY, Fernway, Florist Farms and Heavy Hitters, which makes this a vape-first shop with a solid pre-roll bench. The entry price is $5.31 for Layup's fast-acting raspberry tea, limeade and lemonade cans and Ayrloom's rosé-style 1:1 drink. The Flowery runs several New York stores; this is the only Brooklyn one. Grams on Graham Avenue, a few blocks north, is the better stop for Florist Farms, and Gotham Domino on the waterfront is the larger overall menu.
know: About 350 products from 59 brands; vapes (104) and pre-rolls (95) lead.
Jaunty, STIIIZY, Fernway and Heavy Hitters make it the deepest vape stop in east Williamsburg.
Entry price is $5.31 for Layup fast-acting cans and Ayrloom rosé.
Grams and Sunflower are nearby; Gotham Domino is the larger Williamsburg menu.

faq.q: Which Williamsburg dispensary has the most vapes?
faq.a: Among the six we track, The Flowery Brooklyn is near the top with 104 vape listings, with Jaunty, STIIIZY and Fernway the main brands. Gotham Domino lists more products overall, so check both if you want a specific cartridge.

faq.q: What does fast-acting mean on the Layup cans?
faq.a: Layup drinks use water-soluble THC, which many people feel within 15 to 30 minutes rather than the hour or more a standard gummy can take. Each can is 10 milligrams, and they are $5.31 before tax here.

faq.q: Is The Flowery Brooklyn near the L train?
faq.a: Yes. The Grand Street L stop is a few minutes' walk west along Grand Street, and the Graham Avenue stop is about the same distance north.

intro: Grams Cannabis is at 360 Graham Avenue in Williamsburg, near Conselyea Street and a block from the Graham Avenue L station. It carries about 350 products from 56 brands, the third-largest of the six licensed dispensaries we track in the neighborhood. The menu is evenly split: 85 edibles, 83 pre-rolls, 78 vapes and 71 flower options, plus a 23-item concentrate case that is the largest in Williamsburg.

The defining feature is Florist Farms, stocked at 63 products, the deepest run of that New York brand at any licensed dispensary we track. Jetty Extracts, BLOOM, Jeeter and the shop's own Grams house label fill out the top of the brand list. The entry price is $5.31 for Layup raspberry and mango tea cans, Tune's Sicilian lemon and rose seltzer and Muz Muz two-pack gummies. If Florist Farms pre-rolls or vapes are what you buy, there is no better single shelf in the city.
know: About 350 products from 56 brands, balanced across edibles, pre-rolls, vapes and flower.
63 Florist Farms products, the deepest selection of that brand anywhere we track.
23 concentrates, the largest case in Williamsburg, with Jetty Extracts among the brands.
Entry price is $5.31 for Layup, Tune and Muz Muz.

faq.q: Why does Grams carry so much Florist Farms?
faq.a: With 63 Florist Farms listings, it stocks roughly a fifth of its whole menu from that one New York brand, covering pre-rolls, vapes, edibles and flower. No other licensed dispensary we track comes close, so it is the place to compare the full line.

faq.q: What is Grams, the brand?
faq.a: Grams lists its own house-label products alongside the other brands, about 15 listings under the Grams name. House labels are usually priced below equivalent branded items.

faq.q: Does Grams have concentrates?
faq.a: Yes, 23 listings, which is the largest dab and live resin case among the Williamsburg shops we track. Jetty Extracts is one of the main concentrate brands stocked.

intro: Greene Street is at 3448 Nostrand Avenue in Sheepshead Bay, near Avenue U and a short walk from the Avenue U B and Q station. It stocks about 340 products from 64 brands and is the smallest of the three licensed dispensaries we track in the neighborhood. The mix is balanced: 98 pre-rolls, 82 flower options, 80 vapes and 66 edibles, with a small eight-item concentrate case.

Ayrloom and STIIIZY lead the brand list at 32 and 31 products, with Off Hours, To The Moon, Fernway and Wyld behind them. The entry price is $6 for Ayrloom's single-serve 2:1 drinks in lemonade, half-and-half, orange creamsicle and black cherry. Sheepshead Bay is unusually well served for southern Brooklyn: Twenty8gramz and Quality Control both list far more product within a mile, so Greene Street is the convenient stop near Avenue U rather than the deepest menu.
know: About 340 products from 64 brands, balanced across pre-rolls, flower, vapes and edibles.
Ayrloom and STIIIZY are the deepest brands at 32 and 31 products.
Entry price is $6 for Ayrloom 2:1 drinks.
Twenty8gramz and Quality Control, both nearby, carry much larger menus.

faq.q: How does Greene Street compare to Twenty8gramz?
faq.a: Twenty8gramz lists more than 1,200 products against Greene Street's 340, so it wins on selection. Greene Street is closer to Avenue U and the B and Q, and carries STIIIZY and To The Moon, so it is worth a stop if those brands are what you want.

faq.q: Does Greene Street sell flower?
faq.a: Yes, 82 listings, with To The Moon among the growers stocked. Pre-rolls are slightly deeper at 98.

faq.q: Is there parking?
faq.a: Sensei does not track parking. Nostrand Avenue near Avenue U has metered street parking, but confirm with the shop. The Avenue U station is a few blocks away if you are coming by subway.

intro: Urban Leaf is at 977 2nd Avenue in Midtown East, near 52nd Street and a few blocks from the 51st Street 6 and Lexington Avenue E and M stations. It lists about 340 products from 53 brands, one of the smaller licensed menus among the seven Midtown dispensaries we track. Edibles lead at 118 listings, then 97 vapes and 80 pre-rolls. Flower is a thin 17, and there are 14 concentrates.

STIIIZY is the top brand at 32 products, with Florist Farms at 26, Ayrloom, Jaunty, Jeeter and Heavy Hitters following. The entry price is $5.65 for Jaunty's Dreamberry sleep gummies and sour watermelon two-packs and nama's Sleep Plus and Relax Plus gummies. Urban Leaf is the only licensed shop we track in Midtown east of Madison, which makes it the practical choice for the Turtle Bay and Sutton Place side. For flower, Qube on Broadway lists more than 20 times as many options.
know: About 340 products from 53 brands; edibles (118) and vapes (97) lead, flower is only 17.
STIIIZY and Florist Farms are the deepest brands at 32 and 26 products.
Entry price is $5.65 for Jaunty and nama gummy two-packs.
Only licensed dispensary we track in Midtown East; Qube and Torches are the nearest larger menus.

faq.q: Does Urban Leaf have flower?
faq.a: Very little, 17 listings. The menu is built around edibles, vapes and pre-rolls. If loose flower is the goal, Qube on Broadway or Torches on 42nd Street are the closer Midtown options with real selection.

faq.q: What are the cheapest items at Urban Leaf?
faq.a: Two-pack gummies at $5.65 before tax from Jaunty and nama, including sleep-focused formulas with CBN. They are a low-commitment way to try a brand before buying a full bag.

faq.q: Is Urban Leaf near the UN or Sutton Place?
faq.a: Yes. It is on 2nd Avenue at 52nd Street, about a ten-minute walk from the United Nations and a few blocks west of Sutton Place.

intro: Green Klub is at 108 South Street in the Financial District, on the East River side near the Seaport and a short walk from the Fulton Street transit hub. It is the smaller of the two licensed dispensaries we track in FiDi, with about 300 products from 49 brands. Edibles dominate at 113 listings, followed by 94 pre-rolls, then a modest 42 vapes and 31 flower options, with 12 concentrates.

The brand list is unusual. Dumbo Electric, a Brooklyn label, is the deepest at 28 products, with Grön, Lion Order, Off Hours, Hashtag Honey and LEVEL following. The entry price is $5 for LEVEL's Energy and Slumber five-milligram protab two-packs, with Cycling Frog seltzers in black currant and ruby grapefruit at $6. Highest Standards on the west side of FiDi lists more than twice as many products, so Green Klub is the pick for the Seaport side and for edibles and pre-rolls rather than vapes or flower.
know: About 300 products from 49 brands; edibles (113) and pre-rolls (94) are the core.
Dumbo Electric is the top brand at 28 products, with Grön and Lion Order behind.
Entry price is $5 for LEVEL protabs; Cycling Frog seltzers are $6.
Highest Standards, across FiDi, is the larger licensed alternative.

faq.q: What is Dumbo Electric?
faq.a: A Brooklyn-based New York cannabis brand that Green Klub stocks more deeply than any other label, at 28 products. It covers pre-rolls and flower, which is where most of Green Klub's non-edible depth sits.

faq.q: Is Green Klub near the Seaport?
faq.a: Yes. South Street runs along the East River, and the shop is a few blocks south of Pier 17 and the Seaport district, and a short walk from Fulton Street.

faq.q: How does it compare to Highest Standards?
faq.a: Highest Standards lists about 770 products against Green Klub's 300, with a much larger vape and flower selection. Green Klub has the deeper edible shelf for its size and is closer to the river and the Brooklyn Bridge approaches.

intro: The Flowery's SoHo store is at 481 Broadway, between Broome and Grand, in the middle of the main shopping stretch and close to the Canal Street and Spring Street stations. It lists about 300 products from 54 brands, the third-largest of the four licensed dispensaries we track in SoHo. Vapes lead at 87 listings, with 72 edibles, 69 flower options and 62 pre-rolls. Concentrates are minimal at five.

Heavy Hitters is the deepest brand at 18 products, followed by Ayrloom, STIIIZY, Fernway, PAX and Wyld, a lineup that confirms the vape focus. The entry price is $5.31 for Ayrloom's 2:1 drinks in Honeycrisp, orange creamsicle, yuzu citrus and half-and-half. The Flowery runs several New York stores; this one is the smallest of the Manhattan locations. The Travel Agency on Broadway a few blocks north carries more than twice the products, so The Flowery SoHo is the quicker stop for a cartridge or a drink mid-shopping.
know: About 300 products from 54 brands; vapes (87) are the largest category.
Heavy Hitters, STIIIZY, Fernway and PAX supply the vape depth.
Entry price is $5.31 for Ayrloom 2:1 drinks.
The Travel Agency SoHo, a few blocks north on Broadway, is the larger menu.

faq.q: Which SoHo dispensary is best for vapes?
faq.a: By brand depth, The Flowery SoHo is a strong choice with Heavy Hitters, STIIIZY, Fernway and PAX across 87 listings. The Travel Agency on Broadway lists more products overall, so compare both for a specific cartridge.

faq.q: Is this the same company as the other Flowery stores?
faq.a: Yes. The Flowery operates licensed dispensaries in SoHo, the East Village, the West Village, the Upper West Side, Chinatown and Williamsburg. Each has its own menu, and the SoHo store is one of the smaller ones.

faq.q: Can tourists buy here?
faq.a: Yes. Any adult 21 or older with valid government photo ID can buy at a licensed New York dispensary, including visitors from other states and countries. You cannot take cannabis across state lines or onto a flight.

intro: Sunflower Cannabis Dispensary is at 377 Metropolitan Avenue in Williamsburg, near Havemeyer Street and a few blocks from the Lorimer Street L and Metropolitan Avenue G stations. It carries about 270 products from 42 brands, the fourth-largest of the six licensed dispensaries we track in Williamsburg. Pre-rolls lead at 90 listings, with 69 vapes, 55 edibles and 50 flower options. There are only three concentrates.

Ayrloom is the top brand at 20 products, with Dogwalkers at 18, then MFNY, Nanticoke, Florist Farms and STIIIZY. Dogwalkers, a mini pre-roll brand, is part of why the joint selection runs deep for a shop this size. The entry price is $5 for Ayrloom drinks in vanilla cola, black cherry, lemonade and Honeycrisp. Grams and The Flowery Brooklyn, both within a ten-minute walk, list more product, so Sunflower is the convenient choice for the Lorimer side of the neighborhood or for Dogwalkers specifically.
know: About 270 products from 42 brands; pre-rolls (90) lead the menu.
Dogwalkers mini pre-rolls and Ayrloom drinks are the deepest lines.
Entry price is $5 for Ayrloom 2:1 and 1:1 drinks.
Grams, The Flowery Brooklyn and Gotham Domino are all nearby with larger menus.

faq.q: What are Dogwalkers?
faq.a: A pre-roll brand known for small, multi-pack joints meant for a short session. Sunflower stocks 18 Dogwalkers products, one of the deeper runs of that brand in Brooklyn, within its 90 pre-roll listings.

faq.q: Does Sunflower have concentrates?
faq.a: Barely, with three listings. For dabs or live resin in Williamsburg, Grams on Graham Avenue has a 23-item case a few blocks away.

faq.q: Which subway is closest?
faq.a: The Lorimer Street L and Metropolitan Avenue G share a station a few blocks east of the shop. The Bedford Avenue L is about a ten-minute walk west.

intro: Verdi's Park Slope store is at 360 7th Avenue, near 10th Street and a block from the 7th Avenue F and G station. It is the smaller of the two licensed dispensaries we track in Park Slope, with about 235 products from 52 brands. Edibles lead at 76 listings, then 72 pre-rolls, 38 vapes and 25 flower options, plus 14 concentrates and five each of topicals and tinctures.

MFNY is the deepest brand at 22 products, with Cannabals, Claybourne Co., urbanXtracts, 1906 and Nanticoke behind it. The entry price of $3.39 for 1906's two-pack Boost tablets is the lowest at any licensed dispensary we track in Brooklyn, and Harney Brothers' rosemary yuzu shot, Layup black cherry lemonade and Ayrloom rosé are all $5.65. Be. on Flatbush Avenue has the bigger flower and vape selection in the neighborhood; Verdi Park Slope is the pick on the South Slope side and for edibles, concentrates and low-dose options.
know: About 235 products from 52 brands; edibles (76) and pre-rolls (72) lead.
$3.39 entry price for 1906 Boost tablets, the lowest we track in Brooklyn.
MFNY is the top brand at 22 products; 14 concentrates for a shop this size.
Be. on Flatbush Avenue is the other Park Slope dispensary, with more flower and vapes.

faq.q: What is the cheapest cannabis product in Park Slope?
faq.a: 1906 Boost tablets at Verdi Park Slope, listed at $3.39 before tax for a two-pack. 1906 makes low-dose swallowable tablets in several formulas, and Verdi stocks 13 of them.

faq.q: Is Verdi Park Slope good for flower?
faq.a: Not especially, with 25 listings. Be. on Flatbush Avenue has about four times as many. Verdi's strengths are edibles, pre-rolls and a 14-item concentrate case led by MFNY.

faq.q: Is the store near the F train?
faq.a: Yes. The 7th Avenue F and G station is about a block away at 9th Street, and the shop is on 7th Avenue just south of it.

intro: The Garden Club is at 277 Smith Street in Carroll Gardens, near Degraw Street and a few blocks from the Carroll Street F and G station. We group it with the Brooklyn Heights and Downtown shops, where it is the third-largest of four, with about 210 products from 55 brands. Edibles lead at 80 listings, with 65 pre-rolls, 26 flower options and 24 vapes, plus a handful of concentrates, tinctures and topicals.

The brand list is long for the stock size. Ayrloom is the deepest at 13 products, then Florist Farms, MFNY, Wizard Trees, 1906 and Harney Brothers, with Wizard Trees adding a high-end New York flower option. The entry price is $5 for Ayrloom cran-apple and black cherry cans, Layup black cherry lemonade and Harney Brothers' focus coffee shot. For a bigger selection, Buzzy on Court Street is a ten-minute walk north; The Garden Club is the closest licensed shop for Carroll Gardens, Gowanus and the south end of Cobble Hill.
know: About 210 products from 55 brands; edibles (80) and pre-rolls (65) lead.
Wizard Trees and Harney Brothers are stocked alongside Ayrloom, Florist Farms and MFNY.
Entry price is $5 for Ayrloom, Layup and Harney Brothers drinks.
Buzzy NY on Court Street is the nearest larger licensed menu.

faq.q: Is The Garden Club in Carroll Gardens?
faq.a: Yes. Smith Street at Degraw is in Carroll Gardens, on the Cobble Hill border. Sensei groups it with Brooklyn Heights and Downtown because those are the nearest other licensed shops, but it is the only one in Carroll Gardens itself.

faq.q: What is Wizard Trees?
faq.a: A New York flower brand with a reputation for premium indoor strains. The Garden Club lists eight Wizard Trees products, which is a notable share of its 26 flower listings.

faq.q: Does The Garden Club carry vapes?
faq.a: Yes, but only 24 listings. For a wider cartridge selection in the area, Buzzy on Court Street carries about three times as many, with Fernway and Rove stocked.
